articles.title: The Ephemeris
articles.summary: This December 2024 issue of "The Ephemeris" highlights several astrophotography achievements by amateur astronomers. It features Bryan Marahashi's capture of a lunar occultation of Saturn, Alex Kanaes' extensive mosaic of the Sadr Region in Cygnus, and Francesco Meschia's image of Comet C/2023 A3 Tsuchinshan-ATLAS. Additionally, the back cover showcases Carl Svensson's detailed photograph of the Andromeda Galaxy, with each entry providing equipment and capture specifics.

articles.title: Member Programs
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) offers various member programs designed to support and educate amateur astronomers. These include a library, a free telescope fix-it service, and a 'Quick STARt' program for beginners. Members can also utilize an equipment loaner program and participate in both an Astro Imaging Special Interest Group (SIG) and hands-on astrophotography workshops and field clinics.

articles.title: Public Programs
articles.summary: The 'Astronomy 101' program offers monthly sessions for beginner astronomers, led by Carl Svensson. These sessions cover topics from 'what's up in the night sky' to telescope basics and are held in conjunction with first quarter moon In Town Star Parties at Hogue Park. Attendees also receive a guided sky tour and opportunities to view celestial objects through SJAA telescopes.

articles.title: SCHOOL STAR PARTY
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) offers various observing sessions, including "star parties" for schools across mid-Santa Clara County and monthly public "In-Town Star Parties" at Houge Park in San Jose. Additionally, SJAA hosts solar observing sessions, led by Wolf Witt, typically on the first Sunday of each month at Houge Park, weather permitting. Details for all events are available on their respective websites or Meetup page.

articles.title: Announcements
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) has launched an online apparel store offering branded merchandise, perfect for holiday gifts. Larry Zurbrick has assumed the role of president, succeeding Aroon Nair. Additionally, Marianne Damon recently represented SJAA in an interview on KKUP radio.

articles.title: From The SJAA President
articles.summary: The SJAA President welcomes readers to a new column, commending members for their dedication in sharing astronomical knowledge at public outreach events and star parties. The President also raises a critical concern regarding the lack of succession planning for Program Coordinators and encourages members to consider stepping up into assistant leadership roles, emphasizing the need for long-term commitment.

articles.title: Board Minutes
articles.summary: These board minutes cover updates from September through November 2024, detailing progress on new membership forms and successful community outreach events, including the Santa Cruz Museum's First Friday and a STEM program at Morgan Hill Library. The board also discussed potential collaborations with Astro Revolution and the ongoing process of finalizing a Mendoza Ranch permit contact person.

articles.title: Join Hubble's Night Sky Challenge
articles.summary: NASA is launching "Hubble's Night Sky Challenge" in 2025 to commemorate the Hubble Space Telescope's 35th anniversary, inviting amateur astronomers to observe various celestial objects. Participants can compare their ground-based observations with Hubble's images and earn monthly "silver" or annual "gold" certificates and pins for meeting specific observation and outreach requirements. This year-long program aims to connect amateur and professional astronomy while encouraging skygazing and public engagement.

articles.title: SJAA 70th Anniversary Potluck
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) celebrated its 70th anniversary with a potluck dinner at Houge Park, featuring a variety of delicious food and a communal atmosphere. The event honored current and former members, including guests of honor Robert Garfinkle and Robert Fingerhut, who shared historical anecdotes and stories from the club's past. Attendees also enjoyed a trivia game highlighting SJAA's distinguished membership and accomplishments, such as members having astronomical objects named after them and the club sponsoring the first Cal Star Party.

articles.title: Observing Highlights
articles.summary: This article highlights key astronomical observing events from December through February, including planetary oppositions for Jupiter, Mars, Venus, and Mercury's greatest elongation, providing optimal viewing times. It details major meteor showers such as the Geminids, Ursids, and Quadrantids, noting viewing conditions and dates for the December Solstice, as well as New Moon and Full Moon phases.

articles.title: Kids Corner
articles.summary: This 'Kids Corner' article features a word search puzzle with terms related to comets and space, including Kuiper Belt, Oort Cloud, and various comet parts. It also provides 'Fun Facts' about comets, describing them as cosmic snowballs of frozen gases, rock, and dust that grow a giant glowing head and tail when they approach the Sun.

articles.title: SJAA Recent Events
articles.summary: The article details various recent events hosted by the San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA), focusing on public outreach and education. These included solar observing sessions, a comprehensive telescope workshop, monthly public star parties at different locations, and "Astronomy 101" talks. Additionally, SJAA conducted an online Beginner's Astronomy Forum to answer questions for new enthusiasts, with a timeline highlighting events from September to November.

articles.title: Results from Our Satisfaction Surveys!
articles.summary: This article reports on the satisfaction survey results for public activities held at Houge Park from April 1 to September 30, 2024, fulfilling contractual obligations with the City of San Jose's PRNS. Across 21 public events like Astronomy 101 and Solar Observing, participants gave 100% good or excellent ratings for services and facilities, though the San Jose zip code goal was not met. The report also acknowledges staff and volunteers for data collection and announces a future initiative to automate sign-in sheets and surveys using QR codes.

articles.title: School Star Party Award
articles.summary: Jon Anderson and SJAA were recognized by the Fremont PTA with an award for their contributions through the School Star Party Program (SSP). This award signifies the strong interest in the program and the gratitude from Fremont schools, students, and teachers. The article congratulates Jon and all volunteers for their efforts in making the SSP a success.

articles.title: Swap Meet Recap
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) successfully revived its popular swap meet on September 15, 2024, at Houge Park, marking its first such event since before the pandemic. Author Rob Jaworski notes the event satisfied a significant demand for exchanging astronomy gear and fostering social connections among members and the local community. The club plans to reinstate the swap meet as a biannual event, held once in the spring and again in the fall each year, celebrating the SJAA's 70th anniversary.

articles.title: Spot the King of Planets!
articles.summary: The article celebrates Jupiter as the "King of Planets," detailing its immense size, mass, and significant gravitational influence on the solar system. It highlights how easily Jupiter and its four Galilean moons can be observed from Earth with modest instruments, echoing Galileo's historical observations and even providing an observing tip for December 15, 2024. Furthermore, it discusses the ongoing success of NASA's Juno mission in studying Jupiter's interior and moons, alongside future missions like Europa Clipper.

articles.title: C/2023 A3 Tsuchinshan-ATLAS
articles.summary: The article details observations and astrophotography of comet C/2023 A3 Tsuchinshan-ATLAS by club members, showcasing images captured from June to October. Visible to the naked eye after its September 27th perihelion, the comet was considered a 'great comet' comparable to NEOWISE and Hale-Bopp. Members like Francesco, Yu Li, Rajah, Ed Wong, and Carl Svensson contributed diverse images, capturing its tail and development through various stages.
